Comment: What the API function may reach. Created once by the account owner as a
customer-managed policy, because the deploy deliberately cannot grant it.
Why the owner and not the deploy: a release that can attach an arbitrary policy
to a role it can create, and pass that role to Lambda, can run anything as an
administrator. So the deploy may attach exactly two policy ARNs — the AWS
logs policy and this one — and nothing else. That is one `iam:PolicyARN`
condition in infra/deploy-policy.json, and it is the reason this file exists
separately rather than being written inline by a script.
The function itself holds no provider key and makes no model call. It reads and
writes the session record, the event log and the agent definitions, and reads
the client keys to know whose request it is. When the step worker arrives it
gets a role of its own, with the provider keys, and this one does not grow.

Statement.Comment: Also granted by AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole; repeated so this policy alone is sufficient if the managed one is ever detached.
No CreateTable and no DeleteTable: the function uses the tables, the release makes them. Named, so nothing else in the account is reachable.

Read only, and one secret. The function needs to know whose request this is; it does not need, and must not have, the provider keys — those belong to the step worker, which is a different function with a different role.
